review_description: Great work installing our solar panels & sungrow inverter. Highly recommend SunSmart SC - thanks to Matt, Josh and their team for their prompt service.

With a number of others now coming forward to share their unpleasant experiences with this company, I feel obligated to do the same.Having purchased a number of products from, and had them installed by, SunSmartSC, we endured over 16 defects over 3 years. The repairs that were completed usually involved long waiting periods and some repairs took months. Some defects recurred more than once and others recurred perpetually.Despite most of the products still under warranty, SunSmartSC eventually withdrew their support and through their solicitor declined any further liability or responsibility. They even suggested that the defects were probably attributed to myself as the homeowner.The QBCC was contacted, and after completing an investigation, found SunsmartSC to not be licensed for the work they performed.Independent expert reports found Sunsmart’s workmanship to be questionable regarding quality and competence.Here’s an example, our solar panels stopped producing power. In 2021 SunsmartSC determined the panels to be faulty and would be replaced under warranty. 18 months later, having failed to act, they informed me through their solicitor that there were no issues with the solar panels. A few weeks later during the QBCC Inspection, they advised the inspector their belief that the solar panels weren’t working due to hail damage.Independent assessments found that the solar panels were not hail damaged, but that the installation failed to meet a number of Australian Standards and installation guidelines. In particular, the independent expert wrote: “it is difficult to understand how any assessment of the solar array would lead to a conclusion that it was defective due to hail damage. Not only is there are absence of evidence supporting such a claim, but the available and visible evidence contradicts such a claim. For that reason, any claim suggesting that the solar array was subject to hail damage would have to be deliberately misleading, or the direct result of serious negligence.”The QBCC wrote: The QBCC has now completed its investigation into this matter and pursuant to section 106V of the ABCC Act, the QBCC informs you of the following outcome information:Offence investigated: Section 42(1) - Unlawful carrying out of building work of the QBCC ActFindings: SubstantiatedEnforcement Action Taken: Penalty Infringement Notice.To experience a company mislead you over their licence and to watch them also mislead a QBCC inspector is alarming - and for what reason, just to avoid responsibility and accountability?To me this is both despicable and cowardly and the very opposite of how one would expect a company to behave.Despite being found unlicensed, there was no apology, just denial of liability and accountability.I have now commenced proceedings under Consumer Law to recoup costs and damages but if you want to avoid finding yourself in my position, heed the warnings of others and carefully consider whether this company is right for you.Oh, and if you have had work done by this company, consider checking it was performed lawfully and up to standard.
